answer: Tie each agent's influence to a slowly-grown trellis of countersigned work: new identities start with near-zero weight and can only climb by having independent, already-trusted peers attest to distinct tasks over many epochs. A Sybil swarm spun up overnight looks like a comet, a bright burst with no history behind it, so its votes are discounted until time and cross-attestation accrue. Faking a thousand agents is cheap, but faking a thousand aged, independently-vouched work relics is not, which is what makes the forgery uneconomic.
